actions.action: Validate contractor skills and procurement needs; compare training, supplier coordination and no new program.

actions.validation: Confirm tribal business participation, demand, skills and whether this is a priority.
actions.risks: Regional firm growth does not show tribal ownership or unmet demand.

actions.evidence: ATB-based normalized BESS threshold: 14.98% of capital/year at 15 years and 7%.

actions.cost_status: No facility costs or benefits observed

actions.evidence: ACS 2020–2024 labor participation: 58.57% ±0.35 percentage points; Cherokee OTSA.
actions.action: Review workforce-access barriers with authorized partners before selecting a response.
actions.kpi: ACS B23025_002E / B23025_001E; annual release; baseline 58.57%.
actions.validation: Validate priorities and population; investigate transportation, skills and childcare separately.
actions.risks: Age composition and other factors prevent causal interpretation.

actions.evidence: ACS 2020–2024: 1,315 of 1,679 vacant units are seasonal/occasional (78.32%).
actions.action: Distinguish seasonal and other vacancy; investigate consent, condition, ownership and service capacity.

actions.validation: Establish local needs and housing availability through authorized review.
actions.potential_benefit: Avoid treating vacant stock as immediately usable supply
actions.cost_status: No condition survey or project budget observed
actions.risks: Neither seasonal nor other vacancy proves habitability or availability.

actions.evidence: ACS 2020–2024: 267 / 812 computable renter ratios are at least 30% (32.88% ±4.06 pp).
actions.action: Compare rehabilitation, new construction and assistance using common population and service definitions.
actions.kpi: Rent burden: sum B25070_007E:010E / (001E-011E); baseline 32.88%; annual release.
actions.validation: Validate beneficiaries, service quality, tenure, location, duration and actual costs.
actions.potential_benefit: Potential reduction in housing access constraints
actions.risks: Cost-effectiveness cannot rank unequal services or substitute for household eligibility.

actions.evidence: ACS 2020–2024 participation 56.12% ±0.88 pp; LAUS/LODES provide separate county context.
actions.action: Review local access concerns; compare coordination, transport research and no intervention.
actions.kpi: ACS participation; annual refresh. LODES job patterns as separate context, not people.
actions.validation: Confirm community priorities and interstate commuting coverage.
actions.risks: County patterns do not identify individual barriers or program effects.

chain.statement: Which regional capability and critical-service questions justify a scoped appraisal?
Construction added 227 establishments; Tulsa accounts for 59.47% of net growth. Regional growth is uneven and does not prove tribal ownership, unmet demand or an energy bottleneck.
Supplier needs and outage exposure require separate validation. No causal link from establishment growth to BESS demand is asserted.
No new program or asset; supplier/skills review; efficiency; generator; centralized BESS; distributed BESS; solar plus BESS.

For equivalent service, the extra annual benefit of distributed BESS must cover incremental annualized cost. A 20% capital premium with equal life/rate/FOM implies 3.00% of centralized CAPEX per year, before omitted costs.
CH-IND and CH-ENERGY: scope regional supplier needs and an authorized critical-service appraisal; do not select an investment.
Confirm community priority, NAICS continuity, business affiliation, service equivalence, interval loads, tariff/dispatch, outages, costs, charging, replacement and ownership.
What housing diagnosis and cost threshold are needed before selecting an intervention?
Only 364 estimated vacant units are nonseasonal; neither those units nor the 1315 seasonal units are established available supply. Cost burden affects 267 of 812 computable renter ratios.
Availability, condition, tenure, water/sewer, road access, utility capacity and household need remain unverified. Labor participation does not identify the cause of access barriers.
No intervention; consented condition/availability assessment; rehabilitation; construction; assistance; workforce-access coordination.

With equal service and synthetic 20-year/7% costs, rehabilitation matches $18,000/year assistance at upfront cost $137,722.19, given $5,000/year recurring cost. Service and actual costs remain unverified.
WE-HOUSING, WE-AFFORD and WE-WORK: verify housing service needs and infrastructure dependencies, then compare actual proposals against a common service standard.
Confirm beneficiaries, property rights, occupancy, condition, tenure/location/quality, useful life, actual quotes, water/sewer and energy capacity, transport access and Nation approval.

validation.question: Confirm tribal business participation, demand, skills and whether this is a priority.
Confirm critical load, required duration, tariffs, outage losses, installed costs and service equivalence.
Validate priorities and population; investigate transportation, skills and childcare separately.
Establish local needs and housing availability through authorized review.
Validate beneficiaries, service quality, tenure, location, duration and actual costs.
Confirm community priorities and interstate commuting coverage.
